data.narrative:
Irradiant Technologies, a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Daniel Oran and Amos Meeks, has raised $8.5M to date. The valuation assessment draws from a comp universe of nine private robotics firms (including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI) and one public comparable (277810.KQ), though peer-level triangulation proved limited by data constraints.

Only one valuation method proved applicable: stage-progression analysis. Using the $8.5M capital raised as a proxy for current value and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of Seed-to-Series A step-ups, this method yields $21M. A peer-median approach was not viable—while ten same-sector companies exist, fewer than three fell into sufficiently narrow filters (same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier) to support reliable benchmarking.

The triangulated range spans $18M (low) to $24M (high), with $21M as the central estimate. This analysis carries material uncertainty given reliance on a single method and the absence of tight peer comparables at Irradiant's stage and scale within the Robotics & Manufacturing sector. Validation against future funding events or adjusted peer clustering at adjacent stages would strengthen conviction on this range.
